title: Acceptance thresholds: science core versus JPL Horizons (Sun and Earth seen from the lunar surface)
rule: Written and committed before any Horizons response was compared with the core. This file is not edited afterwards. If a comparison exceeds a threshold, the cause is found and reported; the threshold stays.
applies_to: Every case in cases.json, every row, both bodies, and both computation paths of the core (exact per-site path and site-independent direction table).

direction_arcsec_max.definition: Largest great-circle angle, over all rows of a case, between the apparent direction computed by the core and the apparent azimuth and elevation printed by Horizons (quantity 4).

angular_diameter_arcsec_max.definition: Largest absolute difference between twice the core's angular radius and the angular diameter printed by Horizons (quantity 13).

range_km_max.definition: Largest absolute difference in apparent observer-to-target distance (Horizons quantity 20, converted from au with the IAU value 149597870.7 km).

tdb_minus_ut_seconds_max.definition: Largest absolute difference between the core's TDB minus UTC and the TDB minus UT value printed by Horizons (quantity 30).

known_resolution_of_the_reference: Horizons prints azimuth and elevation in degrees with a fixed number of decimals; the rounding of the reference is reported with the results and is not subtracted from the differences.
